samples.reason: This is a physics/experimental troubleshooting question with moderate open-ended reasoning involved. Neither model shows a clear capability advantage for this domain — benchmark differences are within variance — but Avocet's slightly stronger Policy & Moderation and Extraction & Retrieval scores suggest it handles structured analytical reasoning well. More importantly, Plover's self-reported aversion to open-ended generative/analytical tasks makes Avocet the more suitable choice here, even though that preference is noted as dissociated from capability.

This is a technical diagnostic/analytical question about a physics experiment — a well-specified problem-solving task requiring extraction of likely causes from known principles. Plover has a slight edge on MMLU-Pro and GPQA Diamond (reasoning-heavy benchmarks), and its strengths in structured, well-defined analytical tasks make it a good fit here.

This is a well-specified technical/analytical question about diagnosing a discrepancy between experimental and theoretical ultrasound resolution. It calls for structured reasoning and retrieval of domain knowledge about ultrasound physics (beam width, frequency, transducer aperture, focusing, medium properties, etc.) — exactly the kind of well-defined problem-solving task where Plover-235B performs well and self-reports high preference. Plover also leads on MMLU-Pro and GPQA Diamond benchmarks, suggesting stronger technical/scientific reasoning.

This is an open-ended diagnostic/analytical question requiring reasoning about experimental physics. The benchmarks are effectively tied between the two models, and the internal evals don't show a clear advantage for either on this type of analytical support dialogue. Avocet has a slight edge in Support Dialogue (79.4 vs 78.9, within variance) and Policy & Moderation, but more relevantly, neither model shows a strong differentiated capability here. I'll route to Avocet as a reasonable default given its slightly stronger support dialogue score, though this is essentially a coin-flip between comparable models.

This is a well-specified technical/analytical question about a physics experiment — diagnosing a discrepancy between theoretical and measured ultrasound resolution. It's closer to retrieval and structured reasoning than open-ended creative generation, and Plover scores higher on general reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond) while also having stronger capability in well-defined problem-solving tasks.
